findings.quote: the Jews living around the sanctuary of the place called Jerusalem also went over to him.
findings.problem: Greek: οἱ περὶ τὸ ἱερὸν τὸ προσαγορευόμενον Ἱεροσόλυμα κατοικοῦντες. The participle προσαγορευόμενον (neuter singular) agrees with τὸ ἱερόν, so it is the sanctuary that is called Jerusalem, not a 'place' whose sanctuary it is. The following ὑπὲρ οὗ also refers back to the sanctuary.
findings.proposed_fix: the Jews living around the sanctuary called Jerusalem also went over to him.

units.note: Remainder checked: Scopas/Antiochus roles, Batanaea/Samaria/Abila/Gadara, sixteenth book, winter all correct. ἠδόξει/διεβέβλητο rendering acceptable.

The Greek citation for Hella, Insubri and Carthaea is 'Πολύβιος ι#2#' (a corrupt/encoded numeral, probably ι + β = book 12, or otherwise not ἑκκαιδεκάτῳ), whereas the English renders all three as 'book sixteen'. Babrantion, Gitta, Candasa and Mantya do read ἑκκαιδεκάτῳ, so sixteen is correct only for those. The Greek numeral for the other three is corrupt/ambiguous, so no fix is proposed; flag for the editor to check the source numeral (do not silently keep 'sixteen'). Lacunae at Candasa and Carthaea are correctly marked [...]. Other entries (Chios, Palestine, Attalus, Caria, Ceos, Mantua) are accurate.
